items.title: State cannot deny compensation to rape victims for not producing medical report: Allahabad High Court
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Friday ruled that the State cannot deny financial assistance to rape victims for failing to produce an injury report indicating penetrative sexual assault in cases under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act). A bench of Justice Saral Srivastava and Justice Garima Prasad held that an injury report is not mandatory for receiving the financial assistance under the Uttar Pradesh Rani Lakshmi Bai Mahila Evam Bal Samman Kosh Rules, 2015. The Court therefore quashed a condition that made production of the medical examination report mandatory in cases of aggravated penetrative sexual assault. "Where a medical or injury report is available, it may be placed before and considered by the authority; its absence, however, cannot operate as an absolute bar to monetary relief. The impugned documentary condition is, accordingly, declared unconstitutional and is struck down," the Court ruled The rules provide for financial assistance to women and children who are victims of heinous and violent crimes, particularly sexual offences. items.title: Depression after spouse's death sufficient ground to condone delay in consumer complaint: Delhi Commission
items.summary: The Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission recently held that depression following the death of a spouse can constitute sufficient cause for excusing delay in filing a consumer complaint [Priya Mehrotra v. Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd.]. A Bench of Commission President Justice Sangita Dhingra Sehgal and Member Bimla Kumari made the observation while condoning a 250-day delay in a widow's complaint against Tata AIG General Insurance Company over the rejection of a medical insurance claim. The Commission accepted that the complainant's treatment for clinical depression following her husband's death sufficiently explained the delay. " On perusal of record, we find that there has been a delay of 250 days in filing the Complaint before the District Commission, for which, the Appellant has given sufficient cause, being that she was seeking treatment for clinical depression after the demise of her husband. Therefore, it would be in the interest of justice to condone the delay in filing the Complaint of the Appellant. Having condoned the delay, the District Commission is directed to decide the said Complaint on merits ." the Commission observed. The case arose after Priya

items.title: SEM notice asking Neha Bora to sign peace bond not based on mere hearsay: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday observed that the show-cause notice issued by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) to All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora to execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 and maintain peace was not based on mere "hearsay". Justice Subramonium Prasad observed that the notice was based on the kalandara dated October 17, which consists of the three general diary entries registered at different police stations related to different dates and events. "As such, this Court cannot sit in the armchair of the SEM to test the subjective satisfaction of the sufficiency of material and as to whether the opinion has been correctly been arrived at by the SEM or not," the Bench said. The Court said that the notice, issued under Sections 126 and 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), met the legal requirements for initiating preventive proceedings. The High Court arrived at these findings while dismissing Bora's plea against the notice. However, the Court directed the police to provide all the material to Bora on which reliance will be placed at the time of enquiry and on which basis the notice has been issued. items.title: Judge booked for letting minor son drive Mercedes that killed man in Kochi
items.summary: The Juvenile Justice Board in Ernakulam, on Monday, October 26, granted bail to the 17-year-old son of an Additional District Sessions Judge in connection with a fatal accident in Kochi that killed a scooterist in the early hours of Sunday. The judge has also been booked in connection with the accident, as the Mercedes-Benz sedan involved in the crash was registered in his name. According to police, he has been booked under section 199A(1) (holds the guardian or vehicle owner guilty for an offence committed by a juvenile) and 199A(2) (imposes criminal penalties on the guardian or owner, including up to 3 years' imprisonment and a Rs 25,000 fine) of the Motor Vehicles (MV) Act. The minor, who had initially been let go on station bail under Section 8 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, was taken back into custody due to mounting public pressure and protests by the victim’s family. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has also reportedly been formed to probe allegations made by the victim’s family. items.title: Why Poland wants a stronger relationship with India | The Hindu Editorial
items.summary: Why is Poland seeking a closer partnership with India? Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s visit to India highlighted growing cooperation in trade, technology, defence, critical minerals, renewable energy and geopolitical coordination. With India and the European Union preparing to finalise a landmark Free Trade Agreement, Poland is positioning itself as a key European partner for New Delhi. This editorial explores what both countries stand to gain, the challenges that remain, and why the India-Poland relationship could become increasingly important in Europe’s engagement with India.
